newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea auction prices rise despite big volume.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea auction prices rise despite big volume.

text.p: Colombo auction tea prices rose on widespread demand despite the volume on offer being one of the largest ever, brokers said on Wednesday.

"The overall demand was an indication that prices should move up from now on," said a Forbes and Walker broker. "We're going to see all small sales in February so possibly buyers were trying to buy whatever they can from the large sale."
The expected gross sale average for the 6.0 million kg on offer rose to about 102.50 rupees per kg ($1.78) from 101 rupees last week, Forbes and Walker said.

There was more demand from Britain, Japan and South Africa while Russia, the biggest buyer of Ceylon tea, came in a little more forcefully, perhaps because this week's auction was the last of the large sales, the Forbes broker said.
"Quality compared with the previous two weeks was better," he said. "We're going into the quality season."
The next auction is on February 5 with 4.5 million kg on offer. (1$=57.59 rupees) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
